orchestrator.note: Cost choice: Sol is Codex's recommended default and about 5x cheaper per token than Astra; Astra keeps stage acceptance and Enhanced.

escalateTo.when: the question needs judgment, not search

auditor.game: Round 1 runs every lens. Auditors report everything; the cooperator takes only real findings. A lens with real findings won the round: the same worker fixes, and only winning lenses play the next round. A lens with nothing real lost and is retired for this block. The audit ends when every lens has lost or after the last round; real findings not yet fixed still go to the worker.
auditor.coverage: A lens's round ends only when its auditor returns STATUS: complete (every assigned file read). An auditor that returns STATUS: partial or stops at its limit is continued on its NOT_REACHED files; nothing goes to the worker until every lens in the round is complete. At the token ceiling the lens moves to the next audit tier (workerBudgets.auditors).

economy.selection: Only on the user's explicit choice, launch layer, or standing preference; never chosen automatically.

escalation.requires: For gpt-6-astra above high only: state a concrete unresolved reasoning problem, why high is insufficient, and the expected benefit. Do not escalate solely because a task is large, important, or a prior attempt failed. This exception does not restrict Sol xhigh workers, Luna xhigh roles, or the ordinary worker ladder to Astra high. Explicit user model, effort, and budget limits remain binding.

selectionRules.reuse: Explicit task or launch choice, active task context, or applicable standing preference.
selectionRules.autonomous: Choose Standard for clear solutions or Enhanced for substantial unresolved design; proceed without asking. Applies to unattended execution too.
selectionRules.askOnly: Long-running multi-stage work with substantial unresolved solution choices and material approach/resource impact, with no applicable choice or delegated selection.
selectionRules.runtimeMismatch: Adapt to available settings even for a user-selected preset without a new approval gate. Report material actual routing honestly; separately explicit strict model/effort/budget requirements remain binding.

profileSemantics: Optional, non-exhaustive recommendations. A named choice expresses approach preference, not strict model/effort/team requirements. Custom or unnamed routing is allowed; separately explicit constraints remain binding.

gpt-6-astra.role: most capable; stage acceptance, Enhanced brain, bounded open design

gpt-6.1-sol.role: near-Astra for complex work at Sol price; Standard brain, implementation, block review

gpt-6-sol.status: still served; superseded by gpt-6.1-sol in this policy

gpt-6-luna.role: read-only lookups, mechanical checks, audit lenses at xhigh
gpt-6-luna.effortUpTo: xhigh (max on the API; no ultra)

modelResolution.note: Codex efforts: Astra light by default; Sol and Luna medium by default; ultra enables Codex-native subagents. Config values are low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra.

workClasses.direct: Question, analysis, config or doc edit, or any change the cooperator can already describe exactly, however many files it touches. The cooperator does it inline and runs the project's checks; no agents.
workClasses.build: Fix or feature whose change still has to be found out. One worker block; each audit or review needs its own reason.
workClasses.pipeline: Several unknowns or an open design decision. Plan of blocks with disjoint write sets; stage acceptance only when blocks interact in ways no block review saw.

judging.real: In the diff or caused by it; breaks a quoted rule, document line, or acceptance line at a line that really violates it (the cooperator opens both); reproduces by a check or a concrete scenario.
judging.notReal: Theoretical risk, hypothetical input, work outside SCOPE, taste without a rule, duplicate of a rejected finding; anything the auditor filed under NOTES.
judging.who: The cooperator (orchestrator) judges; auditors and reviewers report everything.

continuity: Fixes go back to the same worker, the next audit round only to the auditors whose lens won the last round, the delta to the same reviewer, through followup_task. A fresh agent is for independence or a different model.

gpt-6-astra.then: the cooperator re-plans or asks the user

workerBudgets.rule: After the third attempt, or when the tool calls or tokens of the block are spent, unfinished work moves to the next tier of the profile's workerLadder as a fresh worker with the original packet, the cooperator's APPROACH, and the HANDOFF only. A submitted block at the limit is verified as it is; a later fix goes to the next tier. At the top of the ladder the cooperator re-plans or asks the user; explicit user limits are binding.
workerBudgets.auditors: A Luna auditor that reaches 400k on a block hands its lens to a fresh Sol xhigh auditor on the same snapshot and round, with its NOT_REACHED files; its findings stay with the cooperator.
workerBudgets.accounting: An attempt is spent only by a run that ends without a result: the worker hit its BUDGET or turn limit, returned STATUS: handoff, or its fix left the finding open. A submitted block, or a fix that closes its finding, spends no attempt. Tool calls and tokens count for every run on the block, fixes included; a HANDOFF-only request is not a new run. Counters stay with the block when it is blocked, submitted, handed off, or put aside.
workerBudgets.usage: Count the new tokens a worker's thread has processed (input minus cached input, plus output), all its runs together; a continued thread keeps counting from its previous total. When the runtime reports no usage, go by attempts and tool calls and say so.
workerBudgets.enforcement: Instruction-level budgets; the runtime does not enforce them.
